pageContent.title: Paul Serban | Software Engineer & Architect
pageContent.author: Paul Serban
pageContent.excerpt: Software Engineer specializing in scalable software architecture, system design, and high-performance full-stack development. I architect resilient systems that deliver measurable business impact.

content.subheading: I am a Software Engineer specializing in system design, software architecture, and full-stack development. I turn complex business requirements into resilient microservices, scalable micro-frontends, and high-performance platforms that drive operational efficiency.

content.text: I build enterprise-grade software, driving the entire lifecycle from initial system design and architectural planning to deployed, scalable solutions. My engineering focus centers on Domain-Driven Design (DDD), CQRS, and building robust microservices and micro-frontend ecosystems.

Whether optimizing AWS cloud infrastructure, containerizing applications with Docker and Kubernetes, or architecting complex integrations, I prioritize measurable outcomes. I have a track record of leading development teams to deliver platforms that significantly reduce time-to-market and cut operational overhead.

Beyond the code, I am an experienced technical coach and team lead. I thrive in collaborative, Agile environments-frequently acting as a solution architect to untangle complex requirements, manage trade-offs (like navigating the CAP theorem), and guide teams to deliver high-quality products under tight constraints.

I am driven by systems thinking in both software and process. I actively explore architectural design patterns and knowledge management techniques, building workflows that streamline development, enforce high technical standards, and ensure continuous team growth.

title.sub: Here is a short list of projects I worked on in order to sharpen my skills.

list.title: Personal Portfolio (V2)
list.subheading: Content-driven Next.js SSG with multi-env CDN delivery
list.excerpt: A Next.js static portfolio that clones a private MDX/JSON content repo at build time, indexes five typed collections through a ContentRepository, ships SEO-ready HTML with sitemap + IndexNow, and deploys preview on GitHub Pages and production on S3 + CloudFront + Route 53.
list.problem: A hand-rolled static site could not keep up with typed collections, cross-cutting tags, SEO compliance, or a clean preview-vs-production release path.
list.approach: Designed a two-repo, build-time content contract - private MDX/JSON cloned into a ContentRepository domain layer, Next.js 13 static export with atomic UI, and branch-gated dual hosting (GitHub Pages preview, AWS prod edge).
list.outcome: Ran as the live personal site for years and established the content-at-build pattern that v3 later evolved into a SQLite pipeline across four surfaces.

list.title: Personal Portfolio (V1)
list.subheading: Vanilla Webpack/Handlebars static portfolio with ADRs
list.excerpt: A purposefully vanilla static portfolio - Webpack 5, Handlebars, and Sass composing JSON-at-build content into a single-page showcase and a first-class design-system page, with GitHub Pages CI and a formal ADR practice.
list.problem: I needed a credible online presence and a freeCodeCamp-compliant portfolio without adopting a framework I could not yet justify - and I wanted the architecture decisions written down, not buried in tribal knowledge.
list.approach: Constrained the stack to vanilla HTML/CSS/JS; treated Webpack + Handlebars as a lightweight SSG over JSON content; split the product into a portfolio surface and a design-system surface; recorded nine ADRs and ASRs as the delivery contract.
list.outcome: Shipped a maintainable static site on GitHub Pages and proved the content-at-build idea that v2 later expanded into typed MDX collections, SEO, and dual hosting.
